ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Selecting the monitoring test

A patient taking stable long-term warfarin has a new interacting medicine added. The clinician plans additional laboratory monitoring to assess anticoagulant intensity. Which test is conventionally used to guide warfarin dosing in this setting?

  1. Prothrombin time expressed as INR
  2. Bleeding time
  3. Anti-factor Xa activity calibrated to heparin
  4. Platelet count alone
  5. Serum thrombin concentration
Answer and explanation

Prothrombin time expressed as INR

INR standardizes prothrombin time for vitamin K antagonist monitoring.

Option explanations

Prothrombin time expressed as INR: INR standardizes prothrombin time for vitamin K antagonist monitoring.

Bleeding time: Bleeding time is not the dosing test for warfarin.

Anti-factor Xa activity calibrated to heparin: Heparin-calibrated anti-Xa testing measures a different anticoagulant effect.

Platelet count alone: Platelet counts do not quantify vitamin K antagonist intensity.

Serum thrombin concentration: Serum thrombin concentration is not the routine clinical monitoring method.
